column1: Mark Rowe reports on the increasingly ambitious geo-engineering projects being explored by scientists
column2: 马克·罗报道了科学家们正在探索的、规模越来越宏大的地球工程项目。

column1: Such is our dependence on fossil fuels, and such is the volume of carbon dioxide already released into the atmosphere, that many experts agree that significant global warming is now inevitable.
column2: 人类对化石燃料的依赖如此之深，排入大气的二氧化碳也已经如此之多，以至于许多专家都认为，显著的全球变暖已不可避免。
column7: released into the atmosphere|排入大气

column1: They believe that the best we can do is keep it at a reasonable level, and at present the only serious option for doing this is cutting back on our carbon emissions.
column2: 他们认为，我们最多只能把升温控制在合理水平，而目前要做到这一点，唯一切实可行的选择就是削减碳排放。
column3: the best we can do|我们最多能做到的

column1: But while a few countries are making major strides in this regard, the majority are having great difficulty even stemming the rate of increase, let alone reversing it.
column2: 不过，虽然少数国家在这方面已取得很大进展，多数国家就连遏制排放增长的速度都十分困难，更不用说扭转增长趋势了。
column3: making major strides|取得重大进展

column1: Consequently, an increasing number of scientists are beginning to explore the alternative of geo-engineering — a term which generally refers to the intentional large-scale manipulation of the environment.
column2: 因此，越来越多科学家开始探索地球工程这一替代途径。这个词通常指有意对环境进行的大规模干预。

column1: According to its proponents, geo-engineering is the equivalent of a backup generator: if Plan A — reducing our dependency on fossil fuels — fails, we require a Plan B, employing grand schemes to slow down or reverse the process of global warming.
column2: 在倡议者看来，地球工程相当于一台备用发电机：如果减少化石燃料依赖的A计划失败，我们就需要B计划，以宏大的工程方案减缓甚至逆转全球变暖。

column1: Geo-engineering has been shown to work, at least on a small localised scale.
column2: 至少在局部的小范围内，地球工程已经被证明能够奏效。
column3: has been shown|已有证据表明

column1: For decades, May Day parades in Moscow have taken place under clear blue skies, aircraft having deposited dry ice, silver iodide and cement powder to disperse clouds.
column2: 几十年来，莫斯科的五一节游行总是在晴朗的蓝天下举行，因为已有飞机撒下干冰、碘化银和水泥粉来驱散云层。

column1: Many of the schemes now suggested look to do the opposite, and reduce the amount of sunlight reaching the planet.
column2: 目前提出的许多方案却想反其道而行，减少到达地球的日照量。

column1: The most eye-catching idea of all is suggested by Professor Roger Angel of the University of Arizona.
column2: 所有方案中最引人注目的一个，是由亚利桑那大学的罗杰·安杰尔教授提出的。
column6: University of Arizona|亚利桑那大学

column1: His scheme would employ up to 16 trillion minute spacecraft, each weighing about one gram, to form a transparent, sunlight-refracting sunshade in an orbit 1.5 million km above the Earth.
column2: 按安杰尔的方案，最多动用16万亿个微型航天器，每个重约一克，在距地球150万公里的轨道上组成一个透明、能折射阳光的遮阳屏。

column1: This could, argues Angel, reduce the amount of light reaching the Earth by two per cent.
column2: 安杰尔认为，这样可使到达地球的光量减少2%。
column6: by two per cent|减少百分之二

column1: The majority of geo-engineering projects so far carried out — which include planting forests in deserts and depositing iron in the ocean to stimulate the growth of algae — have focused on achieving a general cooling of the Earth.
column2: 迄今实施的地球工程项目中，大多数有着同一个目标。这些项目包括在沙漠植树、向海洋投放铁以促进藻类生长等，都着眼于让地球整体降温。
column4: so far carried out|迄今已实施的

column1: But some look specifically at reversing the melting at the poles, particularly the Arctic.
column2: 但有些方案专门考虑如何逆转两极的冰层消融，尤其关注北极。

column1: The reasoning is that if you replenish the ice sheets and frozen waters of the high latitudes, more light will be reflected back into space, so reducing the warming of the oceans and atmosphere.
column2: 理由是，如果能使高纬度地区的冰盖和结冰水域恢复，就会有更多阳光被反射回太空，从而减缓海洋和大气的变暖。

column1: The concept of releasing aerosol sprays into the stratosphere above the Arctic has been proposed by several scientists.
column2: 有几位科学家提出，可在北极上空的平流层中喷洒气溶胶。

column1: This would involve using sulphur or hydrogen sulphide aerosols so that sulphur dioxide would form clouds, which would, in turn, lead to a global dimming.
column2: 按这一设想，使用硫或硫化氢气溶胶，使二氧化硫形成云层，进而让全球接收到的阳光变少。

column1: The idea is modelled on historic volcanic explosions, such as that of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines in 1991, which led to a short-term cooling of global temperatures by 0.5 °C.
column2: 这一设想以历史上的火山爆发为范本，例如1991年菲律宾皮纳图博火山喷发，曾使全球气温短期下降了0.5摄氏度。

column1: Scientists have also scrutinised whether it’s possible to preserve the ice sheets of Greenland with reinforced high-tension cables, preventing icebergs from moving into the sea.
column2: 科学家们还仔细研究过，能否用加强型高张力缆索来保护格陵兰冰盖，阻止冰山移入海中。

column1: Meanwhile in the Russian Arctic, geo-engineering plans include the planting of millions of birch trees.
column2: 与此同时，俄罗斯北极地区的地球工程方案包括种植数百万棵桦树。

column1: Whereas the region’s native evergreen pines shade the snow and absorb radiation, birches would shed their leaves in winter, thus enabling radiation to be reflected by the snow.
column2: 当地原生的常绿松树会遮住积雪并吸收辐射，桦树则会在冬季落叶，使辐射能够被雪面反射回去。
column4: native evergreen pines|原生常绿松树

column1: Re-routing Russian rivers to increase cold water flow to ice-forming areas could also be used to slow down warming, say some climate scientists.
column2: 一些气候学家认为，还可以让俄罗斯的河流改道，让更多冷水流往结冰地区，从而减缓变暖。

column1: But will such schemes ever be implemented?
column2: 但这样的方案真的会得到实施吗？

column1: Generally speaking, those who are most cautious about geo-engineering are the scientists involved in the research.
column2: 总体而言，对地球工程态度最谨慎的，恰是参与研究的科学家。

column1: Angel says that his plan is ‘no substitute for developing renewable energy: the only permanent solution’.
column2: 安杰尔表示，他的计划“不能替代可再生能源的开发；后者才是唯一的长久之计”。

column1: And Dr Phil Rasch of the US-based Pacific Northwest National Laboratory is equally guarded about the role of geo-engineering: ‘I think all of us agree that if we were to end geo-engineering on a given day, then the planet would return to its pre-engineered condition very rapidly, and probably within ten to twenty years.
column2: 美国太平洋西北国家实验室的菲尔·拉什博士对地球工程能发挥的作用同样持谨慎态度：“我想我们都同意，如果有一天停止地球工程干预，地球就会非常迅速地恢复到干预前的状态，大概只需十至二十年。
column6: on a given day|在某一天
column7: pre-engineered condition|工程干预前的状态
column9: within ten to twenty years|在十至二十年内

column1: That’s certainly something to worry about.’
column2: 这当然值得担心。”

column1: The US National Center for Atmospheric Research has already suggested that the proposal to inject sulphur into the atmosphere might affect rainfall patterns across the tropics and the Southern Ocean.
column2: 美国国家大气研究中心已提出，向大气中注入硫的方案可能影响热带地区及南大洋的降雨格局。
column3: National Center for Atmospheric Research|国家大气研究中心

column1: ‘Geo-engineering plans to inject stratospheric aerosols or to seed clouds would act to cool the planet, and act to increase the extent of sea ice,’ says Rasch.
column2: 拉什说：“向平流层注入气溶胶或者播云催化的地球工程计划，会给地球降温，也会扩大海冰覆盖范围。”
column6: extent of sea ice|海冰覆盖范围

column1: ‘But all the models suggest some impact on the distribution of precipitation.’
column2: “但所有模型都表明，这样做会对降水分布产生一定影响。”

column1: ‘A further risk with geo-engineering projects is that you can “overshoot”,’ says Dr Dan Lunt, from the University of Bristol’s School of Geophysical Sciences, who has studied the likely impacts of the sunshade and aerosol schemes on the climate.
column2: 布里斯托大学地球物理科学学院的丹·伦特博士说：“地球工程项目还有一个风险，就是可能‘矫枉过正’。”他研究过遮阳屏和气溶胶方案可能对气候产生的影响。
column4: overshoot|v. 矫枉过正、超出目标
column5: School of Geophysical Sciences|地球物理科学学院

column1: ‘You may bring global temperatures back to pre-industrial levels, but the risk is that the poles will still be warmer than they should be and the tropics will be cooler than before industrialisation.’
column2: “你也许能把全球气温降回工业化以前的水平，但风险在于，两极仍会比应有水平更暖，热带地区却会比工业化以前更冷。”

column1: To avoid such a scenario, Lunt says Angel’s project would have to operate at half strength; all of which reinforces his view that the best option is to avoid the need for geo-engineering altogether.
column2: 伦特说，为避免这种局面，安杰尔的项目只能以一半强度运行。这一切愈发坚定了他的看法：最好的选择，是让我们根本无须诉诸地球工程。

column1: The main reason why geo-engineering is supported by many in the scientific community is that most researchers have little faith in the ability of politicians to agree — and then bring in — the necessary carbon cuts.
column2: 科学界有许多人支持地球工程，主要原因在于，多数研究者不太相信政治人物能就必要的碳减排达成协议，并将其付诸实施。
column5: have little faith in|对……没什么信心

column1: Even leading conservation organisations see the value of investigating the potential of geo-engineering.
column2: 就连主要的自然保护组织也看到了研究地球工程潜力的价值。

column1: According to Dr Martin Sommerkorn, climate change advisor for the World Wildlife Fund’s International Arctic Programme, ‘Human-induced climate change has brought humanity to a position where we shouldn’t exclude thinking thoroughly about this topic and its possibilities.’
column2: 世界自然基金会国际北极项目的气候变化顾问马丁·佐默科恩博士说：“人为气候变化已把人类带到今天这个地步，我们应当认真思考地球工程及其各种可能性，不应把这种思考排除在外。”
column3: climate change advisor|气候变化顾问
column4: World Wildlife Fund’s|世界自然基金会的
column5: International Arctic Programme|国际北极项目
column6: Human-induced|adj. 由人类活动引起的
